chapter.li: LEChapter59 Verse1 Now in the 30th year of the judges’ rule over the Nephites, after Moroni received and read Helaman’s letter, he rejoiced over Helaman’s success in regaining the lands that had been lost. VerseEnd Verse2 He let all his people know throughout the surrounding area so they could also celebrate. VerseEnd

Verse3 Then he immediately sent a letter to Parhoron, asking him to send men to reinforce Helaman, or Helaman’s armies, so he could better protect that part of the land he had so miraculously regained. VerseEnd Verse4 After Moroni sent this letter to Zarahemla, he started to plan how to regain control of the rest of the lands and cities the Lamanites had taken. VerseEnd

Verse5 While Moroni was preparing his plan to battle the Lamanites, the people of Nephihah, who had gathered from the cities of Moroni, Lehi, and Morionton, were attacked by the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse6 Everyone who had fled from Manti and the surrounding area had joined with the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse7 There were many of them, and were reinforced daily by Ammoron’s command, so they attacked the people of Nephihah; and they began to kill them with a massive slaughter. VerseEnd Verse8 Their armies had so many fighters that the rest of the people of Nephihah had to flee from them, and they came over and joined Moroni’s army. VerseEnd Verse9 Now since Moroni expected to send men to the city of Nephihah to keep that city, because it was easier to keep the city from falling into the hands of the Lamanites than to retake it, he thought they would easily keep that city. VerseEnd Verse10 But now he kept all his forces to protect the places he had recovered. VerseEnd

Verse11 When Moroni learned the city of Nephihah was lost, he mourned and began to doubt, because of the people’s wickedness, if they could defeat the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse12 Now all his chief captains also doubted. They were unsure and extremely surprised by the people’s wickedness, assuming this was why the Lamanites succeeded in taking Nephihah. VerseEnd Verse13 And Moroni was angry with the government because of their indifference to the freedom of their country. VerseEnd

LEChapter60 Verse1 He wrote another letter to governor Parhoron. This is what he wrote: I address my letter to Parhoron in the city of Zarahemla, who is the chief judge and the governor over the land, and to all those who have been chosen by this people to govern and support the requirements of this war. VerseEnd Verse2 I have some complaints about 2PP you. 2PP You know 2PP you have the obligation to assemble men and furnish them with swords, cimeters, and other weapons to defend against the Lamanites, wherever they trespass on our land. VerseEnd Verse3 Now I tell 2PP you my men and I, and Helaman and his men also, have suffered tremendously from hunger, thirst, fatigue, and all the difficulties of defending the people. VerseEnd Verse4 But if this were all we suffered, we wouldn’t criticize or complain. VerseEnd Verse5 However, the thousands of our slaughtered people who died by the sword might’ve been spared if 2PP you had given our armies adequate strength and aid. 2PP Your great neglect of us is unexplained. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now we want to know the reason for 2PP your severe neglect. We want to know why 2PP you are so thoughtless. VerseEnd Verse7 Can 2PP you possibly sit thoughtlessly on 2PP your thrones while 2PP your enemies are spreading death all around 2PP you, while they’re murdering thousands of 2PP your fellow Nephites? VerseEnd Verse8 The very people who have expected 2PP your protection, who have put 2PP you in a position of trust to help them? Indeed, 2PP you could have sent reinforcements to them to help them and could have saved thousands of them from dying by the sword. VerseEnd Verse9 But this isn’t all. 2PP You’ve withheld provisions from them, while many have fought and bled to death hoping to protect this people. And they did this when they were about to die from hunger because of 2PP your absolute neglect of them. VerseEnd Verse10 Now, my dearly loved people (because 2PP you ought to be loved by us), 2PP you should’ve acted more diligently to care for and protect the freedom of this people. But 2PP you’ve neglected them, so much so that the blood of thousands will come upon 2PP your heads for vengeance. Indeed, all their cries and suffering were seen by God. VerseEnd Verse11 Could 2PP you possibly think 2PP you could sit on 2PP your thrones and because of God’s great kindness 2PP you could do nothing and He would save 2PP you? If 2PP you have believed this, then 2PP you believed in vain. VerseEnd Verse12 Do 2PP you think that because so many of 2PP your fellow Nephites have been killed, it’s because of their wickedness? I tell 2PP you: If 2PP you have believed this, then 2PP your belief is wrong. I tell 2PP you: There are many who have died by the sword, and it condemns 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse13 Because the Lord tolerates the righteous being killed so His justice and judgment can come upon the wicked. Therefore there’s no need to think the righteous are lost because they’re killed; on the contrary, they enter the rest of the Lord their God. VerseEnd

Verse14 Now I tell 2PP you: I’m very fearful God’s judgments will overtake this people because of their indifference and neglect, including the indifference and neglect of our government and their abandonment of their fellow Nephites who have now been killed. VerseEnd Verse15 If it weren’t for the wickedness that began at the top of our government, we could have defeated our enemies, and they wouldn’t have gained any power over us. VerseEnd Verse16 We’ve been punished because of our own warring between ourselves caused by the kingmen, which resulted in so much slaughter of ourselves. We were fighting among ourselves instead of uniting our strength as we had before. We were divided by the ambitions of the kingmen for power and authority to control us. Instead of being true to the cause of our freedom and joining with us to fight against our enemies, they took up their swords to fight against us. This was what caused so much slaughter among ourselves. If we had instead gone together to defend ourselves with the Lord’s strength, we would have defeated our enemies, since God had promised us that is what would happen, and His word would certainly have been fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse17 But now the Lamanites attack us and are murdering our people with the sword, including our women and children, and removing them as prisoners, afflicting sorrow, distress, and pain, and taking our lands; and this is a result of the great wickedness of the kingmen who are attempting to seize power and authority. VerseEnd

Verse18 But why should I say very much about this? Because it appears likely to us 2PP you are the ones attempting to seize authority. It appears likely 2PP you are also traitors to 2PP your country. VerseEnd Verse19 Or have 2PP you neglected us because 2PP you’re in the heart of our country and surrounded by security, and that’s the reason 2PP you don’t have food sent to us, as well as men to strengthen our armies? VerseEnd Verse20 Have 2PP you forgotten the commandments of the Lord 2PP your God? Have 2PP you forgotten our ancestors were slaves? Have 2PP you forgotten the many times we’ve been rescued from our enemies? VerseEnd Verse21 Or do 2PP you imagine the Lord will repeatedly save us as we idly sit on our thrones and fail to use the resources given to us by the Lord? VerseEnd Verse22 Will 2PP you sit complacently surrounded by thousands of people, even tens of thousands who join 2PP your complacency, while there are thousands around the borders of the land who are dying by the sword, wounded and bleeding? VerseEnd Verse23 Do 2PP you imagine God will consider 2PP you guiltless while 2PP you do nothing but watch these things? I tell 2PP you: No.

Now I want 2PP you to remember God said to first cleanse the inner vessel, and then the outer vessel afterward. VerseEnd Verse24 Now unless 2PP you repent, and start actively sending food and men to us and also to Helaman, so he can maintain the parts of our country that he has regained, and so we can also recover the rest of our lands in these parts, we should stop fighting the Lamanites until we’ve first cleansed our inner vessel, including the top of our government. VerseEnd Verse25 Unless 2PP you start doing what I ask and begin to show me the true spirit of freedom and make the effort to help and support our armies and give them the necessary food for their survival, I’ll leave some of my freemen to maintain this part of our land. I’ll leave the strength and blessings of God upon them, so no other power can work against them VerseEnd Verse26 — and I’ll do this because of their great faith and their patience in their tribulations — VerseEnd Verse27 and I’ll take the fight to 2PP you. And if there are any among 2PP you who have a desire for freedom, if there’s even a spark of freedom remaining, I’ll incite insurrections against 2PP you, up until all those wanting power and authority are dead. VerseEnd Verse28 I’m not afraid of 2PP your power or authority, but it’s God whom I fear. It’s to obey His commandments that I take up my sword to defend the cause of my country. And it’s because of 2PP your iniquity we’ve suffered these losses. VerseEnd

Verse29 It is time, this very moment, that unless 2PP you start defending 2PP your country and 2PP your little ones, the sword of justice won’t just threaten 2PP you, but it will strike 2PP you down in punishment, and 2PP you’ll be destroyed. VerseEnd Verse30 I’m waiting for assistance from 2PP you. Unless 2PP you resupply us, I’ll come against 2PP you, right to Zarahemla, and I’ll strike 2PP you with the sword, and end all 2PP your power to interfere with this people’s defense of our freedom. VerseEnd Verse31 Indeed, the Lord won’t let 2PP you live while 2PP your increasing iniquities are causing the destruction of His righteous people. VerseEnd Verse32 Can 2PP you possibly believe the Lord will spare 2PP you and punish the Lamanites, when their ancestors’ traditions have caused their hatred? And that hatred has grown because of those who have split from us. But 2PP your iniquity is because of 2PP your love of glory and worldly things of no lasting value. VerseEnd Verse33 2PP You know 2PP you’re breaking God’s laws, and 2PP you know 2PP you’re trampling them underfoot. The Lord has told me: If those whom 2PP you’ve appointed as 2PP your governors don’t repent of their sins and iniquities, 2PP you must go up to battle against them. VerseEnd

Verse34 Now I’m obligated, based on the covenant I made, to keep the commandments of God. Therefore I ask 2PP you to obey God’s word and immediately send some provisions and men to me, and to Helaman as well. VerseEnd Verse35 If 2PP you refuse, I’ll immediately come against 2PP you, because God won’t let us die from hunger. Therefore He’ll feed us with 2PP your food, even if the sword must be used. Now see that 2PP you obey God’s word. VerseEnd Verse36 I am Moroni 2PP your chief captain. I don’t seek power, but to pull it down. I don’t seek the world’s honor but the glory of God and the freedom and prosperity of my country. And so I close my letter. VerseEnd
